newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH MINISTRY MAY CEDE POWERS TO BUSINESS GROUP.
newsitem.headline: POLISH MINISTRY MAY CEDE POWERS TO BUSINESS GROUP.

text.p: Poland's economy ministry is considering ceding some powers to the country's chamber of industry and commerce, the economy minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said on Thursday.
He told a news conference that among other prerogatives the chamber could be given powers to grant some import quotas and other foreign trade licences.
The chamber would get these powers if parliament, debating on a draft law on the chamber, decided that firms' membership in the organisation was obligatory, he said.
"Otherwise I will not have a serious partner to talk to. Without the obligatory membership the organisation would resemble a social club," Kaczmarek said.
The business community is divided on whether the long-debated bill on the chamber should introduce mandatory membership in the institution.

Some managers lobby against the solution, fearing the new chamber would be dominated by the current National Chamber of Commerce (KIG) and its leadership rather than by people seleceted democratically.
Many parliamentarian want the new chamber to directly derive from KIG.
